findings: Preserve direct alias/domain references, including forward references, then validate inherited strict records after set memberships exist.
Explicit initialization retains journal/output owners through failure; fixed maximum header admission prevents constructor cleanup ownership loss.
Physical empty scalar streams are checked without writing synthesized logical defaults.
Output plus entire metadata/sort limits receive aggregate disk/handle admission under one root.
Check opened source and pathname, including after output close; ReplaceSource explicitly requires exclusive caller ownership and does not claim CAS/locking.
Membership run validation caches one run rather than looking up its symbol for every row; metadata/name scans still have documented superlinear cost.
Protected inherited metadata, exact duplicate UEL/text slots, prior error counts and full header strings are covered by focused tests.
Publication followed by cleanup failure remains published; errors and abort retry ownership survive without rollback.

An in-flight read failure now fails the borrowing encoder before drop, preserving the sticky primary error and attached cleanup diagnostics; the new regression fails against the earlier b7e09ad import path.

limitations: No append OS/RSS/throughput or general-input scale qualification; task 031 remains pending.
Native GDX interoperability runs on Linux; Rust transaction/fault/feature/corpus suites are separately qualified on four native platforms.
No raw-block passthrough; canonical little-endian re-encoding with selected codec, strict-record rereads and potentially quadratic metadata work.
Immutable-source and exclusive-pathname contract; length/mtime checks are not cryptographic identity or a race-free competing-writer CAS.
Directory fsync/power-loss recovery, filesystem ownership/ACL preservation, and portable fallible-close reporting are not claimed.
